## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the optional JSON argument before merge because placing bare `--json` before a valid `--junit` option aborts report generation. This review assessed coverage by reading the tests.

## Changes

The pull request adds `--json` with a default destination of `results.json` or an explicit path, along with a helper that writes reports to the selected destinations.

## Critical

- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Keep following flags out of the JSON path — `--json --junit report.xml` consumes `--junit` as the JSON path and then rejects `report.xml` as an unknown option. Without `report.xml`, the parser accepts `--junit` as a filename and skips JUnit path validation. — Putting bare `--json` before a valid `--junit` option prevents both reports from being written. — Fix: Apply the same `--` prefix check used for JUnit before consuming an explicit JSON path.

## Important

- app/cli.py:29 — tests — Cover writing both reports in one call — A `write_reports` call with explicit JSON and JUnit destinations has no test that exercises both loop iterations. The only writer test supplies one JSON destination. — A regression that writes only one report when both explicit destinations are supplied would pass the current tests.
